text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PAGER-8242 triggered: canary cluster eu-prod-c1 high p99 latency on /v1/generate (started at 05:12 UTC)

julia: seeing the canary graphs — p99 jumped to ~1.6s, baseline 180ms. errors stable but latency tail bad.
matt: rolling canary deploy v2026.03.14-4 landed about 05:04, 10% traffic. suspect recent KV-prefetch change.
ben: confirmed. logs show repeated GC stalls on worker nodes around 05:10. sample stack: `runtime: gc background mark termination` then long latencies.
julia: @matt can we gate that feature flag for canary? ff:kv_prefetch=true is the new flag. set it false for canary only?
matt: yes — creating flag swap now. plan A: toggle ff:kv_prefetch -> false for eu-prod-c1. plan B: revert single commit if swap doesn't help.
deploy-bot: exec: `redwoodctl flags set --env eu-prod-c1 kv_prefetch=false --reason "canary p99 regression"`
deploy-bot: OK — flag change applied to canary (eu-prod-c1). Monitoring for 2 min.
ben: graphs improving at 05:18 — p99 down to ~210ms. looks promising.
julia: good. need to assess customer impact during the spike. any downstream 5xx or user-facing errors?
matt: error rate stayed ~0.01%, no customer-visible errors reported. affected metric: tail latency impacting timeouts for a small set of long-seq embeddings jobs (3 customers), retries triggered.
julia: write quick note for ops postmortem and customer comms: "short burst of elevated p99 latency for canary due to new kv prefetch gc pressure; mitigated by flag swap; no data loss; minor retries for a handful of jobs."
ben: creating temp incident ticket INC-2026-8242 with timeline and graphs. also pinned the offending commit: `commit abcde12345` (kv-prefetch change).
matt: opening PR to revert single commit as a precaution for next rollout: `revert: abcde12345` -> PR #3287. I'll keep it small.
julia: SRE note — we should keep canary at 10% until next deploy, don't roll forward. Also run heap profiling on canary nodes. @sre-backup can you take that?
sre-backup: on it, starting `pprof` captures now. will attach heap diff.
deploy-bot: Canary flag swap stable for 15m, no follow-up regressions.
ben: ops follow-up: schedule hotfix window in 30 min if PR #3287 approved. prefer a revert single-commit hotfix to avoid reintroducing prefetch until we optimize.
matt: PR opened, tagging @julia and @ben for review. small patch — if approved I'll merge and trigger hotfix release.
julia: approved. go ahead once tests green. coordinate a quick canary verif and then full roll.
matt: running CI. patch merged at 05:37 (merge commit f6a1c). triggering hotfix release: `redwoodctl deploy --tag hotfix/revert-abcde12345 --target eu-prod`
deploy-bot: Hotfix deployment started. Canary: eu-prod-c1 (10%), eu-prod-c2 (10%).
incident-bot: Note: Paging rotation — julia is primary, ben second, see on-call schedule.
ben: monitoring hotfix rollout. initial canary p99 back to baseline. starting full rollout at 05:46.
julia: customer impact summary for CS: "Brief p99 latency spike affecting a small number of long-sequence embedding jobs in EU. No errors reported, automatic retries handled most cases. Root cause: KV-prefetch GC pressure in new prefetch implementation; mitigated by flag swap and single-commit revert. Full fix in progress."
matt: full rollout completed at 05:52. post-rollout telemetry shows stable p50/p95/p99.
ben: arch note for postmortem: add GC tuning, limit prefetch concurrency, and add automatic canary memory ceiling.
sre-backup: uploaded pprof heap snapshots and flame graphs to INC-2026-8242.
julia: closing action items: (1) postmortem draft, (2) customer comms, (3) follow-up fix to prefetch implement. I'll hand off to ben for night ops runbook updates.
ben: acknowledged, taking handoff. marking incident resolved in PagerDuty. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PAGER-8242 resolved (ack closed) at 06:05 UTC
